div.p: Mixed-criticality system (MCS) is one of the upcoming and most challenging research areas in embedded systems. Real-time (RT) scheduling for MCS is a key aspect done during design time to analyze the schedulability and strictly guarantee the timing of various critical tasks. This paper tries to study if the existing non-MCS preemptive scheduling approach for periodic and aperiodic tasks can be extended to uniprocessor MCS. A comparison between the maximum response time for the tasks in a non-MCS and MCS is performed. It is inferred that the conventional preemptive scheduler is sufficient but does not give minimal response time for a high critical task. This provides the groundwork to further explore and contribute to the research area.

div.head: INTRODUCTION
div.p: One of the recent areas of research in RT systems is the design of a mixed critical system. MCS existed prior to the emergence of the concept as a challenging research topic in 2007. In ARINC653 standard with avionics RT systems and integrated modular avionics (IMA) architecture, the requirement for integration of platforms for a shared resource, while avoiding interference by isolation was imposed. Earlier a federated architecture was used with independent resources for the individual module, but it was understood sharing resources reduces cost, power consumption and with minimization of interference helps to increase the safety aspect of the system. The IMA architecture is a distributed RT system with multiple functionalities implemented with various systems across the sub-systems. Same sub-systems contain functionalities with a diverse level of criticality. To address these issues of IMA architecture, the MCS was proposed with RT characteristics by Vestal et al. [1].

In 2007, Vestal et al. introduced how to extend standard fixed priority (FP) RT scheduling concept for single processor MCS using Response Time Analysis [1]. Then, Audsley's optimal priority assignment algorithm [1] was found to be more optimal for MCS than rate monotonic and deadline monotonic priority assignment algorithm. Further, Baruah et al. tried fixed job-priority scheduling and dynamic priority scheduling for sporadic tasks [2]. Many studies have been conducted recently wherein the researchers have succeeded in reducing the response time for high-critical tasks at the expense of lowcritical tasks failing to meet their deadlines. This is when some of the tasks enter high-critical mode and all low-critical tasks will be rejected to dedicate all the resource to meet the timing constraints of high-critical tasks. To overcome such challenges, Baruah et al. in [3] tried to reduce their execution and response time with the introduction of the MC task model with degraded quality. Baek et al. [4] developed schedulability tests for nonpre-emptive scheduling which can be modified to pre-emptive scheduling in uniprocessors systems. In this paper pre-emptive scheduling for periodic and aperiodic tasks is used to further analyse the behaviour of MCS.

Guaranteeing timing of the MC tasks is one of the key challenges faced during the design phase. Certification authorities help in guaranteeing the correctness of an MCS, under extremely harsh assumptions which results in large worst-case execution time (WCET) for high-critical tasks. These requirements of integration of the platform together with a reduction in the WCET of high-critical tasks with reliability and safety lead to the complexity of the design of RT scheduling for MCS. RT scheduling for MCS is a key aspect done during design time to analyse the schedulability and strictly guarantee the timing of various critical tasks without degrading the other critical task performance. In this paper, the concept of MCS, significance of feasibility and schedulability for pre-emptive scheduling for periodic and aperiodic tasks have been discussed; opening avenues to further explore and contribute to the research. The algorithm is validated with a synthetic task set generated using UUnifast algorithm [5] and log-uniform distribution [6].

The remaining paper is organized as follows. In Section I the MCS and the related works in the area of RT scheduling of MCS is discussed, followed by section II which introduces to the system design and section III expound the methodology. Then in section IV the results obtained are examined and section V concludes the paper by stating the possible future scope.

div.head: D. Acceptance Test
div.p: Schedulability, requirements on resources, the level of criticality of aperiodic tasks lead to a significant step in the design phase of the algorithm since they occur at runtime. When an aperiodic task arrives at runtime, the acceptance test is used to handle and guarantee its schedulability without considerably altering the schedulability of previously guaranteed tasks. In the acceptance test, the availability of sufficient resources and feasibility with respect to other guaranteed tasks are determined. If a task is accepted, the resources it requires is reserved and will be available during its schedule. Various algorithms can be employed to guarantee the reservation of resources. Further, to reject a resource, multiple rejection strategies are employed to ensure the cost of rejection is less than the cost incurred if the task is not executed. This gives WCET and deadline for low and high critical tasks. The task parameters generated are stored in a task parameter matrix. But whenever task shifts to high-critical level, the WCET, is high-critical WCET, while deadline is high-critical deadline . Feasibility test is performed using demand bound function for the offline tasks. During runtime, if an aperiodic task arrives, its task parameters with arrival time is noted [10]. div.head: III. METHODOLOGY AND DESIGN OF SCHEDULING ALGORITHM
div.p: The designing of the pre-emptive scheduling algorithm for MCS follows a procedure of steps:

1) Identification of the appropriate method for MC-RT scheduling. In this paper, scheduling is done using pre-emptive scheduling where the tasks with minimum absolute deadlines are scheduled first [11].
2) A system model is defined according to the chosen approach where the terminologies and notations for various parameters are defined.
3) Generate synthetic tasks for MCS using UUnifast algorithm and log-uniform distribution.

4) Schedulability of a set of MCS tasks with specific task parameters is ensured using the feasibility test. In this design, low critical tasks are not schedulable below a stated lower bound, and a high critical task is not schedulable beyond a stated upper bound. 5) Acceptance test for all aperiodic tasks is performed as it arrives at runtime.

6) The schedulable task with a minimum deadline is considered at each tick so as to ensure that tasks do not miss their deadlines. 7) When two tasks are eligible to be scheduled at a tick, then the tasks with more criticality is chosen for scheduling. 8) Further, the waiting time of the task also reflects on the task chosen for scheduling.

Thus, the design of pre-emptive scheduling algorithm for MC tasks with periodic and aperiodic nature is performed and simulation of the algorithm is done on MATLAB. The algorithm is validated using the synthetic task-set.

div.head: E. Comparing MCS and non-MCS task scheduling using preemptive scheduling
div.p: In Table V, the maximum response time taken by tasks in an MCS and non-MCS is given. The comparison shows that the pre-emptive scheduling used for non-MCS can be used to schedule the MCS tasks, but there is no improvement in the response time for high-critical tasks. Thus, it is sufficient but not efficient scheduling algorithm for MCS.

div.head: V. CONCLUSION
div.p: In this paper, the RT scheduling for the MCS is analysed for periodic and aperiodic tasks. The design of conventional preemptive scheduling is extended to an MCS with periodic and aperiodic task models. The feasibility and acceptance tests are redesigned to accommodate the impact of criticality levels on the system. Synthetic task sets are generated using UUnifast and log-uniform distribution to verify the algorithm. It is inferred that the conventional pre-emptive scheduler is sufficient to schedule mixed-criticality tasks. But the algorithm fails to give better performance and better response time for critical tasks. This limitation of the conventional scheduling algorithm for an MCS is to be mitigated with further research. A probabilistic scheduling approach can be introduced to incorporate the effect of level of criticality and provide a better response time for the high critical tasks and better performance for the MCS.
